sentences.text: Hon'Ble
Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 25th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Civil Case No. 3898 of 2024
 Smt. Sakshi
 Versus
 Aditya
 Appearance:
 Shri Devdeep Singh, learned counsel for the petitio
 Shri Ravindra Upadhyay, learned counsel for the res
 Order

The applicant has filed this application under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for transfer of proceedings of case No.RCSHM 29/2024 from the court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kannod to the learned Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Tikamgarh.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kannod
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Tikamgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The short facts of the case are that the applicant and respondent solemnized marriage on 22.06.2023 by following Hindu customs and traditions.
After marriage, there was dispute between the parties.

As such, a divorce petition was filed by the respondent before the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kannod which was registered as RCSHM 29/2024.
3.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kannod
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner by filing this application submits that the distance between Kannod and Tikamgarh is approximately around 390 km.

There is no direct conveyance available to Kannod from Tikamgarh, therefore, the petitioner has to take train from Tikamgarh to Bhopal and then from Bhopal 2 MCC-3898-2024 to Kannod she has to go by bus.
It is further stated that the taxi service is too expensive which the applicant cannot afford.
She cannot travel alone.
As a lady it is very hard for the applicant to manage the travelling.
She is only a homemaker, therefore, she is totally dependent on her parents financially as well as travelling.
4. It is also submitted that she has instituted a case under Section 144 of BNSS claiming maintenance before the Principal District Judge, Tikamgarh, which is pending consideration.
She has also registered an F.I.R. under Section 498-A, 506 and 34 of IPC r/w Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act at Tikamgarh.
As such the applicant in any case has to travel to Tikamgarh for attending the proceedings in those two cases, thus, he prays for transfer of proceedings to Tikamgrah.

5. While arguing the learned counsel for the petitioner has also referred to a document uploaded in the reference of ERP and has stated that during pendency of the case the father of the applicant has also died.

Learned counsel has also placed reliance on the order of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the Smt. Sakshi vs Aditya on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199847764/
1 case of Sumita Singh vs Kumar Sanjay and another, 2001 (10) SCC 41 and has stated that in view of the said order it is the wife whose convenience is to be kept in mind while dealing with such type of cases.
6.

1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sumita Singh vs Kumar Sanjay and another, 2001 (10) SCC 41
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent points out that the divorce petition was filed on 14.08.2024.

On which date notices were also issued to the applicant and the applicant appeared before the Court at Kannod in the divorce petition on 24.09.2024, however, just one day before appearing she lodged an F.I.R. on 23.09.2024 under Section 498-A etc. at 3 MCC-3898-2024 Tikamgarh.

Then after going back to Tikamgarh, she filed a case under Section 144 BNSS on 21.10.2024 claiming maintenance, he thus, points out that both the proceedings were instituted after receiving notice of divorce petition and after appearing before the Court at Kannod.
As such, he submits it is only a creation of excuse for transfer of proceedings.
He further points out that the applicant is not required to come on each and every date of proceedings before the Court at Kannod.

He then points out by referring to the application filed by the applicant before the Court at Kannod under Section 24 in divorce proceedings particularly para 2 and 3 that, she demanded expenses for travelling for attending court proceedings there at and in the entire application she has not stated that there is no one to accompany her and she is unable to attend the proceedings.
The only demand was of expenses and maintenance pendente lite.
He thus submits that present is only a case for harassing the respondent.

If the proceedings are transferred then the witnesses of the respondents have to travel to Tikamgarh, as he has filed the petition the burden is upon him to prove his case thus he has list of witness who will have to be examined by him and the transfer of application shall create grave hardship in producing his evidence.
He thus prays for dismissal of the application.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

At the outset, it has to be recorded that although the Hon'ble Apex Court in several cases observed that in matrimonial cases convenience of wife has to be looked into, however, after taking into account flood of transfer petitions in such cases, the Hon'ble Apex Court considered this 4 MCC-3898-2024 aspect in the case of Anindita Das vs. Shrijit Das reported in (2006) 9 SCC 197 and observed that "henceforth the cases have to be considered on their own merits".

entities.text: Anindita Das vs. Shrijit Das reported in (2006) 9 SCC 197
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, now this cannot be straight jacket formula that the consideration is to be based only with respect to convenience of the wife.

Hon'ble the Apex Court in the aforesaid case has held in paras 3 to 5 as under :
"3.
Even otherwise, it must be seen that at one stage this Court was showing leniency to ladies.
But since then it has been found that a large number of transfer petitions are filed by women taking advantage of the leniency shown by this Court.
On an average at least 10 to 15 transfer petitions are on board of each court on each admission day.
It is, therefore, clear that leniency of this Court is being misused by the women.
4 . This Court is now required to consider each petition on its merit.
In this case the ground taken by the wife is that she has a small child and that there is nobody to keep her child.

The child, in this case, is six years old and there are grandparents available Smt. Sakshi vs Aditya on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199847764/
2 to look after the child.
The respondent is willing to pay all expenses for travel and stay of the petitioner and her companion for every visit when the petitioner is required to attend the court at Delhi.
Thus, the ground that the petitioner has no source of income is adequately met.
5. Except for stating that her health is not good, no particulars are given.

On the ground that she is not able to come to Delhi to attend the court on a particular date,
she can always apply for exemption and her application will undoubtedly be considered on its merit.

Hence, no ground for transfer has been made out."
9.

In the facts of the present case, this is crystal clear that the divorce petition was instituted and notices were issued on 14.08.2024 and the applicant appeared before the Court in divorce case on 24.09.2024 and after appearing she instituted a case of maintenance on 21.10.2024 at Tikamgarh 5 MCC-3898-2024 and lodged F.I.R. just one day prior of appearing on 23.09.2024 at Tikamgarh under Section 498A.

It is thus clear that the applicant was acting on a design to get the proceedings transferred from Kannod to Tikamgarh, thus, she instituted cases at Tikamgarh after institution of divorce petition and receiving notice of those proceedings.

In her application before the Court at Kannod she had demanded the expenditure for her and for her companion without any whisper of any inconvenience, it is not her case that her application has been rejected.
Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, this Court is not inclined to order for transfer of proceedings from Kannod to Tikamgarh.
Consequentially, the application is hereby rejected.
MCC stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
